label: accepted

evidence.V1: Front and silhouette show a clean regular octagon (A15 X/Y error 0.0) that reads as a chunky token at 64 px; edge-on top view is a thick gold bar with the boss just peeking out, which is the expected coin read from that angle.
evidence.V2: Three clear tiers: big gold octagon rim, medium recessed teal field plus lighter raised inner octagon boss, small cream diamond gem.
evidence.V3: Chunky 0.316/1.75 thickness and heavy rim are stylised, but the diamond gem is small (about 1/7 of the coin width) and very low relief, and the wide plain field makes it read as stacked extruded octagons rather than a confident, exaggerated design.
evidence.V4: Rim close-up shows a consistent outer chamfer band catching light along every segment; the boss and gem edges carry matching small chamfers (light strip on the boss lower-right, gem upper-left); no razor or blobby edges visible.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups are clean: flat-shaded facets are intentional, no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray faceting; emblem penetration (0.06) is hidden and gates A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: Gold accent rim, one hue (teal) in two values (dark field, light boss), cream gem: disciplined with good value contrast; colourways keep the same structure.
evidence.V7: 376 tris against the small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500).
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, kit gold/cream plus one hue in 2 values, chamfered flat-shaded edges consistent with the kit; colourways (crimson, shadow) swap only the hue.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

evidence.V1: Clean octagon outline in front, three-quarter and silhouette renders reads instantly as a coin/token at 64 px; top view is a thick gold disc edge, which is what a coin should be edge-on; A15 symmetry error X=0.0, Y=0.0, emblem offset 0.0, both emblems seated (gap 0).

evidence.V3: Chunky rim and deep recess are pleasantly exaggerated, but the boss and gem are plain flat extrusions; the gem is a thin, small rhombus plate that reads timid against the boss, so the face feels partly primitive rather than confidently stylised.
evidence.V4: Rim close-up shows a consistent chamfer band between front face and side that catches light; boss and gem top edges are chamfered too; no razor or blobby edges.
evidence.V5: Face and rim close-ups (studio and flat) show clean planar faces with no pinches, seams, patches or z-fighting; the 40 cross-shell overlaps are the intentionally inset emblems (0.06 penetration) and show nothing visible; A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: gold accent rim, one hue (teal) in two values for field and boss, warm cream gem; good value contrast; colourways (crimson, shadow) swap only the hue and stay clean.
evidence.V7: 376 tris against a small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500).
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, kit gold/cream plus one hue, chamfered edges and flat smooth shading consistent with the kit anchor.

artifacts: none visible; 40 cross-shell overlaps reported are the intentional emblem seating penetration (0.06 studs), not visible in renders
top_fixes: Make the emblem read stronger: enlarge the diamond (about 1.5x) and give it more relief or a facet split so it carries at 64 px
Break up the wide empty field, e.g. a small inner step ring, notches at the octagon corners, or bring the boss larger so the field band is narrower
Add a matching small chamfer to the rim's inner lip where it drops to the field so all rim edges catch light the same way
Increase chamfers to the kit ~0.045 studs on the rim outer/inner edges, field recess lip and boss so edges catch light consistently
Push stylisation: slight dome or swell on the boss and field, a beveled/faceted gem instead of a flat diamond slab, or a stepped rim profile to move it beyond stacked extrusions
Consider a small secondary detail on the rim (notches or inner bead ring) to strengthen small-scale read at the edge-on angle
Give the gem real presence: thicker, taller faceted gem (pointed bevel or pyramid top) sized up to fill more of the boss, so the small tier reads at 64 px
Add a secondary detail to the field or boss (inner bevel ring, notches or small studs at the octagon corners) so the face is not just stacked flat octagons
Consider slightly softening the rim's outer side edge (second, smaller chamfer) to match the rounder rim read of the kit anchors
